clue.text: Flier the RAF redefined to have failed

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the preceding words are smashed and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An aircraft let down by the air force's revised specifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' and 'RAF' suggest a plane, but the flier is a bird: FEATHERED FRIEND is a jokey name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird flies, and a jocular phrase for any bird is a friend with plumage.

clue.text: Possible employer looks carefully at A-level choice

blocks.note: a business is a firm that may hire you
to study is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A prospective employer scrutinises the subjects a school leaver chose.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are the exams English pupils take at about 18, choosing a few subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Business studies is one of the subjects a sixth-former may pick for exams before university.

clue.text: This may speed through the streets, if I re-engineer part

definitions.text: This may speed through the streets

indicators.note: only a portion of the written phrase is wanted, a run of consecutive letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the second of the first word to just before the final two letters

explanation.surface: A motorist plans to tune a component so the car can race through town.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency vehicles answering a call for help race along roads with sirens blaring.

clue.text: Hangman promoted? The sauce

blocks.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner
moved up in rank

explanation.surface: An executioner gets a promotion, prompting a sharp retort: the cheek of it!
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch's name became a byword for the hangman in England. 'The sauce' reads as cheek or impudence, but it is the tomato condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is the familiar tomato condiment, a sauce squeezed onto chips and burgers.

clue.text: Almost pretty Scottish city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: bonny is the Scots word for pretty

explanation.surface: A Scottish city that is nearly attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish city' looks like the definition, but Scottish belongs to the wordplay; the city is German, the former West German capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonn is a city on the Rhine that served as the West German seat of government.

clue.text: Sadly lament holiday not operational, given health crisis

indicators.note: something going sadly is going wrong, so the word that follows is put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
a break is a short holiday
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Someone grieves that a holiday fell through and their health suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse of psychological wellbeing is an acute personal crisis of health.

clue.text: Being taken in, isolation is path for treatment

indicators.note: material that gets treatment is processed and altered, so the letters before are reworked

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient admitted to a ward finds solitude is the route to recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being admitted to a ward is being taken in as an inpatient for care.

clue.text: Elvis due to reincarnate? Unreal!

indicators.note: reincarnation brings something back in a new form, so the letters return rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan expects the King of rock and roll to be reborn, and a sceptic scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory, based on a false belief, has no basis in reality.

clue.text: Dear church members, you need a cat here

blocks.note: as in the exclamation 'O dear!'
Church of England
a lot is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: A vicar's letter to the congregation says they need a cat in the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear church members' reads as the opening of a letter, but Dear is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted feline of Central and South America.

clue.text: A band of zebras?

blocks.note: surface reading: a herd or musical group made up of zebras
setter's reading: a band is a strip of colour, one of many on the animal's coat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a collective noun for a group of animals; it is a single line of colour on the hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra's coat consists of alternating black and white bars of colour.

clue.text: War memorial not cheap to rebuild

indicators.note: rebuilding puts something together again differently, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Restoring a monument to the fallen will be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cenotaph in Whitehall, London, is Britain's national war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument honouring dead soldiers whose bodies lie elsewhere.

clue.text: Some blame Zeus for Greek food

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the next words are wanted, a consecutive run across them

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Diners blame the king of the gods for their Greek meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meze are small dishes of appetisers served in Greek and Turkish cooking.

clue.text: The Swiss state is in N Italy, true? False

indicators.note: a false version is not the genuine one, so the preceding letters are put in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims Switzerland lies in northern Italy, and is told that is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Swiss state' looks like the country itself, but it is the condition Switzerland is famous for.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is known for its long-standing policy of taking no side in wars.

clue.text: Unveiling the final book in the series

definitions.text: the final book in the series

blocks.note: first meaning: a disclosure of something hidden

blocks.clueFragment: the final book in the series
blocks.note: second meaning: the last book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A launch party marks the closing volume of a book series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The series' sounds like a run of novels, but it is the Bible, whose last book is this.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising disclosure is a revelation, and the Book of Revelation closes the New Testament.

clue.text: Part of a summer shower, in itself regularly mild

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the Latin phrase per se means in itself
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A light summer rain shower that is gentle in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer shower' suggests rain; the Perseids are a meteor shower peaking each August, and one meteor of it is a Perseid.
explanation.definitionFit: A single meteor from the August Perseid stream is one member of that celestial shower.

clue.text: Work garment more than a couple of pounds

blocks.note: over means in excess of
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them

explanation.surface: Workwear that costs above two quid.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a loose protective coat or one-piece suit worn over clothes while working.

clue.text: Extract bus ticket and get on

blocks.note: a bus pass lets you travel
getting on is growing older

explanation.surface: Take out your bus ticket and board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' reads as boarding the bus, but it means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt quoted from a book or piece of music is a passage.

clue.text: Eccentric or angry, as Humpty ended up

blocks.note: first meaning: wildly unconventional, or in informal use furious
second meaning: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall

explanation.surface: Someone describes the nursery-rhyme egg as mad or cross after his tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-wall is an idiom for bizarre or zany, and literally describes where Humpty fell.

clue.text: Primate burying saint in rear of church

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A monkey buries a holy man at the back of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop in a church setting, but here it is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Lifting weights with this a breeze, to a girl

blocks.note: a breeze is a light wind
lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone tells a girl that pumping iron with this gadget is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting weights' suggests a gym, but the weights are heavy loads such as anchors, and 'a breeze' does double duty as the ease it brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch with a crank and drum used to haul up loads such as anchors.

clue.text: Colleague that puts an end to a lot of adverbs

definitions.text: that puts an end to a lot of adverbs
definitions.note: describes a suffix, not a noun for a person

blocks.note: first meaning: a partner or associate

blocks.clueFragment: that puts an end to a lot of adverbs
blocks.note: second meaning: the ending of words such as basically and finally

explanation.surface: A coworker who stops people overusing adverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter on your side, and many adverbs close with this four-letter suffix.

clue.text: So far, fox fed itself

blocks.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: Up to now, the fox has fed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up until the present moment, a synonym for thus far.

clue.text: Where every country can obtain water for the sick?

blocks.note: the United Nations, where every nation is represented
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A question about where every nation can get water for its ill people.
explanation.walkthrough: The UN is the United Nations, nearly every country being a member.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwell and sick are synonyms describing someone in poor health.

clue.text: Racing here, great deal?

blocks.note: good as in 'a good deal', meaning large
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether going racing is a great bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is a racecourse in West Sussex, England. 'Great deal' reads as a bargain, but deal is a kind of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwood is a famous English racecourse that hosts the Glorious Goodwood meeting each summer.
